t: The Yangshao people farmed millet, and some rice, along the middle Yellow River and kept pigs and dogs; over two thousand years their region became a fully settled farming society.
Their potters, working without a wheel, made fine painted wares whose fish, face and geometric designs changed over time and spread west to the Majiayao culture and beyond.
Villages of houses round a central square were joined in the later phases by settlement hierarchies, large public buildings and, at Xishan, the first rammed-earth wall in China.
dyk: A dragon figure from the Yangshao culture, dating to the fifth millennium BCE, is the world’s oldest known depiction of a dragon.
ev: The Early Yangshao, or Banpo phase, begins, with villages such as Banpo and Jiangzhai in the Wei River valley
A dragon figure is made that is the oldest known depiction of a dragon
In the Middle Yangshao, or Miaodigou phase, the culture and its population expand in all directions
The Late Yangshao begins, with settlement hierarchies spreading and the first rammed-earth wall in China built at Xishan
The Majiayao culture, which grew out of the middle Yangshao through an intermediate Shilingxia phase, begins to the west
Johan Gunnar Andersson discovers the Yangshao site in western Henan, which gives the culture its name
The Yangshao culture is estimated to be more than 1,000 years older than the Anau culture, weakening Andersson’s theory of a western origin

f.homeland: The middle reaches of the Yellow River in China, mainly Henan and the neighbouring provinces of Shaanxi and Shanxi. Key sites: Yangshao (Mianchi County, Henan), Banpo near Xi’an, Jiangzhai, Beishouling, Dadiwan, Xishan near Zhengzhou and Xipo.
f.period: c. 5000–3000 BCE: Early Yangshao or Banpo phase c. 5000–4000 BCE, Middle Yangshao or Miaodigou phase c. 4000–3500 BCE, Late Yangshao c. 3500–3000 BCE.
f.known: millet farming; pig keeping; painted pottery with human faces, animals and geometric designs; jiandiping amphorae; ditch-enclosed villages; semi-subterranean houses; millet and rice beer; the first rammed-earth wall in China; the oldest known depiction of a dragon
f.sources: Excavated settlements and burials since 1921; pottery styles and stratigraphy (the Hougang site); residues and tools; studies of diet. No writing: marks on pottery at Banpo and Jiangzhai have been read by a few as numerals or early signs, a reading not widely accepted.
